title: The Uncharted Wreck
premise: Ada Galloway, a mountain guide blacklisted after a rescue gone wrong, is hired by a desperate widow to find the survey expedition that vanished upriver while hunting the wreck of the Meridian, a colonial-era ship rumored to hold stolen heirlooms. Racing a salvage fleet with legal claim to the site, Ada discovers the expedition's leader alive — and that he is the man whose testimony destroyed her career. Over six tides, she must choose between delivering him to justice, selling him to the fleet, or trusting him as they raise the wreck and expose the corruption that ruined them both. In the end, the wreck's true cargo — evidence, not gold — clears her name, but she lets him go free, choosing love over the justice she finally holds in her hands.
about_author: S. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former river-boat deckhand who spent a decade guiding expeditions through remote coastal ranges before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for taut survival plots and characters who carry their pasts like ballast.

chapters.title: The Last Contract
chapters.summary: Ada Galloway, working under a false name at a coastal outfitter, is tracked down by Elena Vasquez, whose husband's survey expedition went silent eleven days ago upriver. The salvage fleet has already filed claim on the wreck site. Ada refuses, then finds Elena has proof of who betrayed her years ago. POV: Ada. Beat: reluctant ignition — she takes the job out of spite, not hope.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ada provisions a shallow-draft boat and studies tide tables: six high tides before the fleet's cutter reaches the wreck channel. She recruits Tomas, a teenage mechanic with his own debts, and slips past the harbor patrol at night. A radio fragment from the missing expedition plays — a voice she recognizes. POV: Ada. Beat: momentum and dread; the clock starts audibly ticking.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Upstream, Ada finds the expedition's abandoned camp: ransacked tents, a torn chart marking the wreck, and signs of a fight. Tomas deciphers the chart while Ada reads boot prints — someone walked away alive, heading into the mangroves. That night a fleet scout plane passes low overhead. POV: Ada. Beat: unease deepens; the mystery turns personal when she spots familiar gear.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed the Report
chapters.summary: In a stilt hut, Ada finds Julian Marsh — expedition leader, and the man whose false testimony got her blacklisted. He claims he recanted, that the original report was buried by the same company now backing the salvage fleet. He was left for dead by his own crew. POV: Ada, with a flashback to the hearing. Beat: fury versus doubt; old wounds reopened at knifepoint.

chapters.title: Fleet Water
chapters.summary: The fleet's advance team arrives early, led by Captain Ilsa Brandt, who offers Ada a clean record in exchange for handing over Marsh and the chart. Ada stalls, learns the fleet plans to dynamite the wreck rather than excavate it — destroying whatever evidence it holds. POV: Ada, with a tense negotiation scene. Beat: temptation made concrete; the enemy shows its face.

chapters.title: Dead Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ada, Marsh, and Tomas navigate a flooded side-channel to reach the wreck before the fleet, losing most of their supplies when the boat grounds. Marsh saves Tomas from drowning, cracking Ada's armor further. They reach the Meridian's exposed hull at dead-low tide. POV: alternating Ada and Marsh. Beat: grudging trust forged in shared danger; the wreck looms like a verdict.

chapters.title: The Cargo Below
chapters.summary: Inside the flooded hold, they find no treasure — instead a sealed strongbox of documents proving the shipping company trafficked stolen heirlooms and framed its own captains, including the man whose report damned Ada. The tide begins rising; the fleet's demolition barge appears upstream. POV: Marsh, revealing his guilt and his recantation letter hidden aboard. Beat: revelation — the wreck itself is the witness.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide
chapters.summary: Brandt's boarding party storms the wreck. In a running fight through collapsing corridors, Tomas is captured and the strongbox nearly lost. Ada trades herself for Tomas, buying time, while Marsh escapes with the documents toward the last seaworthy skiff. POV: Ada, captive on the barge. Beat: sacrifice and despair; duty to others costs her everything again.

chapters.title: The Wreck Speaks
chapters.summary: Marsh broadcasts the documents' contents on the fleet's own frequency, forcing Brandt's corporate backers to stand down rather than be implicated. Ada breaks free during the chaos and confronts Brandt as the demolition charges — already armed — begin to flood the Meridian. POV: Ada and Marsh converging. Beat: climax; justice arrives sideways, through exposure not law.

chapters.title: Slack Water
chapters.summary: The Meridian settles into the mud, its secrets published worldwide. Ada's name is cleared; the blacklist collapses. Brandt is arrested, but Ada chooses not to press charges against Marsh, letting him walk — love against duty one final time. On the sixth tide, she and Tomas sail home past the wreck's masthead breaking the surface. POV: Ada. Beat: resolution — stillness earned, moving forward without running.
